style: 3D animated (Pixar-style CG) for 0-41.67 s; hard cut to live-action handheld phone 'real me' flex clips 41.67-44.0 s. Yellow italic word-by-word captions with black outline, centred at ~45% height.
logline: A rich couple bicker while botching their own Ferrari wash; a teen in a rusty junk car offers to do it, makes it spotless, gets paid, turns word of mouth into a detailing company, and three years later rolls up in a McLaren to tell the husband he was busy getting paid.

hook.mechanic: Opens mid-argument (a scream in the first 0.3 s), then the underdog is introduced by a deadpan jump-cut pair in his rust bucket, publicly ridiculed ('In that junk car?') and answers with a dare ('Just watch'). Conflict + underdog + challenge inside 5.5 s; the viewer stays to see him prove it.
hook.first_line: You're scratching it! / Then you do it!

montage.description: Two wordless 'satisfying clean' montages in macro: spray -> brush -> pressure jet -> matched before/after frame on the same wheel, foam, panel rinse, microfibre wipe, vacuum, then a glossy beauty shot. The first sells skill (one car); the second (after 'Girls, you need my detailer!') sells growth: a new car every ~1 s (BMW, Porsche, Lamborghini), then branded van, handshake deal, employee in matching uniform, smile to camera. Ends on a white flash into 'THREE YEARS LATER'.

stats.dead_air: None: continuous music bed (no silence at -35 dB/0.4 s); loudness flat at about -14 LUFS momentary for 0-41 s, rising to about -10/-11 for the live tag. Dialogue gaps: 5.3-14.2 (8.9 s, montage 1), 19.5-35.7 (16.2 s, montage 2 + time jump + arrival).

beats.summary: HOOK: couple screaming over a botched Ferrari wash; teen in a junk car offers, is mocked, says 'Just watch'.
PROOF montage: macro detailing, dirty -> clean match frames, beauty shot.
Reaction + reward: 'Wait... What?!', $350 paid, Nate's delighted '350?', wife recommends him to friends.
GROWTH montage: more supercars, branded van, handshake deal, employee, smile to camera.
Time jump: white flash, 'THREE YEARS LATER' on a purple McLaren; he signs for it and drives to the villa.
PAYOFF: husband (now washing his own car) asks how; 'You were busy arguing. I was busy getting paid.'; laugh, then whip into a screaming ECU 'WHAT?!'.
Real-life tag: real creator's vans, McLaren, stock room, waterfront dinner.

transcription: faster-whisper small (CPU, int8) with word timestamps, cross-checked against the burned-in captions; three lines are from captions only
why_it_works: Status gap set up instantly: villa, Ferrari and suit versus a teen in a rust-streaked car; the ridicule line states it out loud so nobody misses it.
The dare ('Just watch.') is a promise; the next 8 s pay it off visually with no words, so attention never drops.
Macro 'satisfying' detailing with matched before/after frames is watchable on its own, and every cut is a tiny reveal.
A concrete number ($350) makes the win feel real and gives Nate a big readable reaction (eyes pop, grin).
Word of mouth is dramatised in one line ('Girls, you need my detailer!') and turned into a scale-up montage: same action, bigger cars, then van, deal, staff.
Classic time-jump card on a hero object (purple McLaren) after a white flash, then a mirrored return to the opening location.
Payoff line is short, parallel and quotable ('busy arguing / busy getting paid'), delivered from a low seat in the supercar; then a whip into a screaming ECU gives a comic final button.
The CG-to-real tag (the real creator's fleet and car) frames the fable as 'based on a true story' and makes it aspirational.
undetermined: Music not identified (I cannot listen); the loudness shape is measured only.
Husband at the end is redesigned (burlier, cream shirt, lighter hair), probably a model-consistency drift rather than a new character; the dialogue implies it is the same man.
'Let him try.' speaker inferred (husband folds his arms on it).
'How'd you afford that?', 'Hahaha' and the final 'WHAT?!' come from captions only; times estimated.
34.3-41.0 is treated as one shot with a boom/dolly move (checked on a 0.37 s strip); the cut at 41.0 sits inside a whip-blur 40.88-41.25.
